constraints: Risk indicators must not automatically become hard declines.
Missing inputs must not be treated as failed inputs.
Hard-decline rules require explicit policy approval.
Manual review must override automatic positive outcomes.
Every outcome must include rule IDs and explanations.
Eligibility conditions met does not mean loan sanctioned.
A DECLINE resting on a low-confidence (OCR-derived) value becomes MANUAL_REVIEW.
A risk-signal rule (risk_signal=true) can only produce MANUAL_REVIEW and the generic borrower category DETAILS_NOT_VERIFIED.
A rule whose mvp_status is DEFERRED is not evaluated in the MVP; it is kept in the catalogue.

Amount-dependent rules (PL-064, PL-065, PL-108, PL-109, PL-110, PL-118, PL-120, PL-122, PL-123, PL-126) are evaluated at the PL-129 offered amount. A breach at the requested amount alone gives COUNTER_OFFER at the largest passing amount (ADR-0007 #2), never MANUAL_REVIEW and never a referral.

Every product is capped at Rs. 25 lakh in the MVP (ADR-0007 #1). A request above the product cap or the ceiling gets COUNTER_OFFER; above the ceiling it also sets request_outside_mvp_range and the borrower is told it is outside what we offer. Above Rs. 75 lakh (PL-070) it is declined as outside what we offer.
C3 resolved: v2 P05 ('over a product cap: refer') is superseded by COUNTER_OFFER (ADR-0007 #2).

The offer step (PL-129, flat rate per product) runs after the request-independent gates. DECLINE from such a gate wins; under MANUAL_REVIEW the offer is indicative for the underwriter. PL-125 (risk-grade sizing) is DEFERRED (ADR-0007 #3).
DECLINE from an amount-dependent rule happens only when no amount at or above the Rs. 40,000 minimum passes.
ELIGIBILITY_CONDITIONS_MET with eligible_amount < requested_amount, or a changed tenure, is reported as COUNTER_OFFER; it is not a sanction.

counter_offer.basis: largest amount passing every amount-dependent rule
